correctness.rationale: For both alternating reduced Coxeter words, Bruhat subwords are exactly the distinct 2^(n-1) permutation vertices. The explicit binary two-coordinate inequality gives upper bounds 18 (interior) and 8 (boundary), with sharp iff conditions; endpoint deviations incur a loss exceeding their possible gain. Summing each of the four parity/order cases proves 9n-19, 9n-18 and 9n-20 exactly. Equality forces all first-layer swaps in both permutations and complementary second-layer swaps; strict convexity excludes nonvertex contacts. The included self-contained checker verifies the local lemma, exhaustive pairs in n=3..10 and larger random witnesses, not a substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This computes a previously unidentified natural extrinsic Euclidean metric invariant for two distinguished families of Bruhat interval polytopes with exponentially many vertices, and classifies the whole diametral graph rather than giving only a bound. The squared Euclidean diameter exhibits a strict orientation-dependent gap of exactly two in even ranks despite equal vertex counts and the fixed 1-skeleton graph diameter n-1. This gives a sharp geometric boundary to the orientation-insensitive combinatorial theorem, beyond a mere restatement or a special-case table.
